name: Proxmox_VE_Node_Detail
description: This node's CPU, memory, uptime, load, swap, root filesystem, pressure stall figures and its own view of cluster quorum, asked of the node itself.
technicalNotes:
Script collection on the node's own resource: three calls to this node per interval -- /nodes/{node}/status, /nodes/{node}/rrddata and /cluster/status. The node is asked directly, at the resource's own hostname, and never through another node, which would answer for itself. A node that does not answer fails the run.

CPU, memory and uptime are the node's own figures, so their alerts are raised, routed and silenced on the node.

LoadPerCore normalises load average by logical CPU count so a single threshold is meaningful across differently sized nodes. Proxmox returns load average values as strings; the script coerces them explicitly.

The Pressure datapoints are Linux pressure stall information: the percent of time some (or, for Full, all) tasks waited for CPU, IO or memory, per-minute averages from rrddata. Pressure is the clearest single measure of a node that cannot keep up. Each is withheld where the node does not report it.

Quorate and NodesOnline are this node's own view of the cluster. Quorate alerts when this node has lost quorum; NodesOnline is recorded without a threshold, since the cluster modules alert on nodes going offline and one copy of that alert per node would bury it. Both are withheld on a standalone host, which has no quorum to lose.

Applies on ProxmoxVE_Node resources the NetScan has not marked unreachable (pve.netscan.reachable). The suite has no addCategory_* PropertySource: the NetScan sets the categories and pve.cluster.role, and the product page lists them for a resource added by hand.

Requires Sys.Audit on /nodes/{node} for status and rrddata, and on / for /cluster/status; the PVEAuditor role includes both.

Units: memory, swap, root filesystem and KSM in bytes, as Proxmox reports them; uptime in seconds. MB and GB are decimal (10^6 and 10^9 bytes); the product page states the suite's convention.

datapoints.name: CPUUsagePercent
datapoints.description: Node CPU utilisation, percent.
datapoints.alertBody:
Proxmox node ##HOSTNAME## is at ##VALUE##% CPU. Its guests are competing for CPU time; consider migrating some to a less busy node.

This started at ##START##, ##DURATION## ago.

datapoints.name: CPUCount
datapoints.description: Logical CPUs available to the node.

datapoints.name: MemoryUsedBytes
datapoints.description: Memory in use, bytes.

datapoints.name: MemoryCapacityBytes
datapoints.description: Total memory, bytes.

datapoints.name: MemoryUsagePercent
datapoints.description: Memory utilisation, percent.
datapoints.alertBody:
Proxmox node ##HOSTNAME## is using ##VALUE##% of its memory. Close to the limit the host starts swapping or killing processes, guests included.

This started at ##START##, ##DURATION## ago.

datapoints.name: UpTimeSeconds
datapoints.description: Seconds since the node booted.

datapoints.name: PressureCPUSomePercent
datapoints.description: Percent of time some tasks waited for CPU, 1-minute average. Withheld where the node does not report pressure.

datapoints.name: PressureIOSomePercent
datapoints.description: Percent of time some tasks waited for IO, 1-minute average. Withheld where the node does not report pressure.

datapoints.name: PressureIOFullPercent
datapoints.description: Percent of time every task waited for IO at once, 1-minute average. Withheld where the node does not report pressure.

datapoints.name: PressureMemorySomePercent
datapoints.description: Percent of time some tasks waited for memory, 1-minute average. Withheld where the node does not report pressure.

datapoints.name: PressureMemoryFullPercent
datapoints.description: Percent of time every task waited for memory at once, 1-minute average. Withheld where the node does not report pressure.

datapoints.name: Quorate
datapoints.description: 1 when this node is part of a quorate cluster, by its own view. Withheld on a standalone host.
datapoints.alertBody:
Proxmox node ##HOSTNAME## has lost quorum. It is cut off from the majority of its cluster: it stops starting, migrating or changing guests until quorum returns.

Status: ##ALERTVALUEDISPLAYSTATUSNAME## (##VALUE##).

This started at ##START##, ##DURATION## ago.

datapoints.name: NodesOnline
datapoints.description: Cluster members online, by this node's own view. Withheld on a standalone host.

datapoints.name: LoadAverage1m
datapoints.description: 1 minute load average.

datapoints.name: LoadAverage5m
datapoints.description: 5 minute load average.

datapoints.name: LoadAverage15m
datapoints.description: 15 minute load average.

datapoints.name: LoadPerCore
datapoints.description: 1 minute load average divided by logical CPU count.
datapoints.alertBody:
Proxmox node ##HOSTNAME## has a load of ##VALUE## per core.

This started at ##START##, ##DURATION## ago.

datapoints.name: SwapUsedBytes
datapoints.description: Swap in use, bytes.

datapoints.name: SwapCapacityBytes
datapoints.description: Total swap, bytes.

datapoints.name: SwapUsagePercent
datapoints.description: Swap utilisation, percent. Sustained swap use on a hypervisor indicates memory overcommit.
datapoints.alertBody:
Proxmox node ##HOSTNAME## is using ##VALUE##% of its swap. Sustained swap on a hypervisor means memory is overcommitted, and every guest on the node slows down.

This started at ##START##, ##DURATION## ago.

datapoints.name: RootFSUsedBytes
datapoints.description: Root filesystem used, bytes.

datapoints.name: RootFSCapacity
datapoints.description: Root filesystem size, bytes.

datapoints.name: RootFSFreeSpace
datapoints.description: Root filesystem free, bytes.

datapoints.name: RootFSUsedPercent
datapoints.description: Root filesystem utilisation, percent. A full root filesystem stops pvedaemon accepting work.
datapoints.alertBody:
The root filesystem on Proxmox node ##HOSTNAME## is ##VALUE##% full.

This started at ##START##, ##DURATION## ago.

datapoints.name: CPUSockets
datapoints.description: Physical CPU sockets populated on the node.

datapoints.name: CPUCores
datapoints.description: Physical CPU cores per socket.

datapoints.name: IOWaitPercent
datapoints.description: Percent of CPU time spent waiting on IO. Sustained IO wait means storage, not CPU, is the constraint.
datapoints.alertBody:
Proxmox node ##HOSTNAME## is spending ##VALUE##% of its CPU time waiting on disk IO. Storage, not CPU, is the bottleneck, and guests on this node will be slow to read and write.

This started at ##START##, ##DURATION## ago.

datapoints.name: KSMSharedBytes
datapoints.description: Memory reclaimed by kernel same-page merging, bytes. Absent when KSM is disabled on the node, which is why it is not reported as zero.
